description:
THIS IS #2944 HALF (b) (Fable, MAIN-READY-9: the version-drift task #2944 owns the LEARNED-facts follow-up; filed here before that message arrived -- work it under #2944, this file is its detail).

FILED s513g (Opus, 2026-10-09) when the #2878 overlay reader landed, as #2878 asked.  NOT designed in detail; this is the shape and the questions.

WHAT EXISTS NOW (s513g): `PCL::Facts::<Module>` overlays -- hand-written forward declarations, read by the same walk as the module's source and merged (fill an absence; a conflict dies naming both files; exports unioned), consumed at the `use` (#2871 positional) and by the module's own unit at its `package` statement (Pl::Parser::_merge_facts_overlay / register_unit_overlay; docs/shipped-modules.md "Facts overlays").  The #2610 detector (`%p-note-sub-install`, PCL_DETECT_TABLE/PCL_DETECT_LOG) already sees, at run time, every compile-phase install whose prototype disagrees with the KIND the compiler assumed at a call site below it.

THE IDEA: at the same hook, when a module unit's compile phase installs a sub the compiler did not know (assumed `unknown` / `builtin`, installed `()` / `(&;@)` / ...), record `(package, name, prototype)` in the module's cache SIDECAR (beside the cached .lisp and its deps file).  On the next transpile of that module -- and of every unit that `use`s it -- the extraction reads the sidecar's records exactly as it reads an overlay (the same merge, same conflict rule), so the call site is parsed right from the second run on, with no hand-written file.  The detector keeps verifying: a learned fact that a later run contradicts is an event, and the learned record is dropped.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE BEFORE BUILDING: (1) the FIRST run still parses wrong -- is that acceptable for a value-changing site (rule 12: the detector's announce flag covers the first run)? (2) A learned fact depends on the RUN (File::Path's `_IS_*` depend on $^O; Sub::Quote's on the perl version) -- the sidecar must key on whatever the install read, or store only the PROTOTYPE (never a value), which is what an overlay does; (3) invalidation: the sidecar is keyed by the module's bytes like the cached transpile, so an edited module forgets; (4) the cache is per user/per root -- an installed tree shares nothing; (5) precedence: a hand-written overlay and a learned record that disagree -> conflict (die) or overlay wins?  MEASUREMENT FIRST: count, over the four populations, the detector events a learned record would have removed on the second run (the s513g AFTER logs list the residue after the hand-written overlays).
subject: LEARNED FACTS (follow-up of #2878): the runtime writes the prototype a compile-phase install REALLY gave a sub into the module cache's sidecar, the extraction reads it on the next transpile as if it were a facts overlay, and the #2610 detector keeps verifying -- so a module's BEGIN-time installs need no hand-written overlay after its first run
